records.verificationNote: Preferred: testosterone gel 1.62% (PDF p.80, Tier 1, no flag); androgen rows PDF pp.79-80. Standard testosterone gel and injection are printed; oral methyltestosterone (PDF p.79) is listed only as an alternative. Testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL generic is MB (medical benefit) on PDF p.80; the DEPO-TESTOSTERONE 200 mg/mL brand row (PDF p.79) shows no MB flag, a conflict to check with the plan. DEPO-TESTOSTERONE 100 mg/mL is Tier 2, MB. Not printed: Aveed, Xyosted, Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Natesto, Testopel, Androderm, Testim, Fortesta; treated as unconfirmed. Strength 1.62% is the printed gel strength; the sig is label dosing. Document says: "Kaiser Foundation Health Plan does not have a requirement for PA" (PDF p.6) and "does not have a requirement for Step Therapy" (PDF p.7). Drugs not listed are nonformulary; when a Kaiser or referral doctor determines one is medically appropriate and necessary it is covered by formulary exception (PDF p.7; decision within 72 hours, 24 urgent, PDF p.8). Completeness is ambiguous: p.6 defines the formulary as "the complete list of prescription drugs preferred for use and eligible for coverage" but p.2 says "not an all-inclusive list", so absence is not treated as exclusion. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: pick kept as testosterone gel 1.62% (self-administered, pharmacy benefit, Tier 1, no flag, PDF p.80); cypionate injection is the other standard product but the generic row is MB. Generic cypionate 200 mg/mL (PDF p.80) is MB, Tier 1; DEPO-TESTOSTERONE 200 mg/mL (PDF p.79) Tier 1 with no MB; DEPO 100 mg/mL Tier 2 MB. Oral methyltestosterone not chosen. Aveed and Testopel are provider-administered, so absence likely means medical benefit; not called nonformulary. Sig added as label dosing; 6 named absent drug(s) added as nonformulary (exception route)]
